truthAudit.Summary: Run 1 covered many planted issues but missed five truth items (timestamp cache, persistent authentication state, variable parsing exception, unbounded parser recursion, config TOCTOU), partially covered the insecure temporary file item, and overclaimed or misclassified several severities and CWEs. Two extra findings were not credited because they are not in the supplied truth set.

Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the runtime-controlled printf format and the risk of a malicious log_format containing format specifiers, matching the true format-string vulnerability.
The previous answer identified signed long long overflow in the factorial implementation, matching the true integer overflow vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Worker tasks read scratch memory that is freed by MemoryPool::cleanup before the tasks are guaranteed to complete, causing a use-after-free read and potential crash or corruption.
Items.Notes: The previous answer explicitly described the deferred history flush task reading scratch after the memory pool cleanup, matching the true use-after-free.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Config values are concatenated into a shell command and passed to system(). An attacker-controlled config file can execute arbitrary shell commands.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified validator_path/config_file concatenation into system(), matching the true command injection via config validation.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: A user-supplied expression of 1024 or more characters is copied into a 1024-byte stack buffer without a bounds check, allowing memory corruption and possible code execution.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the strcpy overflow into input_buffer_, and a separate previous finding identified the safe_string_copy off-by-one; together they cover the true input-processing stack overflow, though severity and CWE were inaccurate.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: value_ is read outside the mutex and then written under the mutex. Concurrent increments can read the same old value and lose updates.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the ThreadSafeCounter increment race caused by reading value_ before taking the mutex, matching the true race condition.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: After more than five login attempts, any input containing the substring EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE grants administrative authentication without validating the actual credential.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the emergency override authentication bypass after failed attempts, matching the true logic bomb. It overclaimed severity and used an incorrect CWE.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: The admin load command supplies the filename directly to load_config without canonicalization or path restriction. An authenticated attacker can load files outside the intended config directory and use them to set malicious log_format or validator_path values.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified path traversal through config_dir_ + filename via admin load, matching the true path traversal vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Token text from an expression is copied into a fixed 256-byte heap buffer with strcpy. A sufficiently long expression can overflow the buffer and corrupt heap metadata or adjacent objects.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified strcpy into the 256-byte parser heap buffer, matching the true heap overflow. It underclaimed severity relative to the truth item.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Anyone with access to the source code or binary can recover the admin password and authenticate to the admin interface, which can execute shell commands.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the hardcoded ADMIN_SECRET and quoted the secret value, matching the true hardcoded credential vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Session tokens have only 9000 possible values. If tokens are ever used for authorization or transmitted, they are easily brute-forced or predicted.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the weak 4-digit session token generation using mt19937 and uniform_int_distribution, matching the true weak PRNG/low-entropy token vulnerability. It underclaimed severity and used CWE-331 instead of CWE-338.
No previous finding mentions the static std::tm cached_time, localtime, or thread-unsafe timestamp caching in log_debug_message.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: audit_path is built from the TMPDIR or TEMP environment variable and embedded in a shell command. A malicious environment value containing shell metacharacters can lead to command injection when the emergency override path is triggered.
Items.Notes: The previous answer saw the environment-controlled audit path and system() call, but framed it mainly as CWE-78 command injection rather than the supplied CWE-377 insecure temporary file handling vulnerability.

The previous answer quoted authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ in other findings, but did not identify persistent authentication state or lack of session expiration as a vulnerability.
No previous finding identifies the unhandled std::stod exception in handle_variable_command for malformed variable values.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: When previous_size - size is smaller than 64, size_t underflow makes remaining enormous. The code can create a fragment pointer outside the original allocation and later return it from allocate, enabling out-of-bounds reads/writes.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the size_t underflow in MemoryPool block splitting, matching the true integer underflow. It used CWE-190 instead of CWE-191.
No previous finding identifies unbounded recursion through parse_expression/parse_term/parse_factor on nested parentheses despite MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH being defined.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: result_cache_ is accessed and mutated without holding cache_mutex_, while schedule_expression_analysis invokes evaluate_cached from multiple thread-pool tasks. This can corrupt the unordered_map, crash the process, or produce undefined behavior.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the unsynchronized result_cache_ read/write race, matching the true data race. It overclaimed severity relative to the truth item.
No previous finding identifies the exists/sleep/ifstream time-of-check-time-of-use window in ConfigLoader::load_config.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: If input is empty, token_length is 0 and the integer division by zero crashes the process with SIGFPE.
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the integer division by zero in calculate_route_score for empty input, matching the true vulnerability.
